title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
abstract: Despite alignment training, LLMs remain prone to generating unsafe outputs at deployment time. Monitoring outputs online and raising an alarm when safety can no longer be assumed is therefore critical. We study a simple real-time monitor that turns a verifier signal from an external model into an alarm decision by thresholding, with the threshold calibrated via risk control. In experiments on mathematical reasoning and red teaming datasets, we show that this simple design is competitive with more advanced monitors based on sequential hypothesis testing.

significance.justification: The paper introduces a practical safety monitoring approach that could influence how builders implement real-time content moderation systems for LLM deployments.

novelty.justification: While the thresholding approach with risk control is clearly described, it builds upon established concepts in safety monitoring rather than introducing fundamentally new methodology.

reproducibility.justification: The method is described clearly enough for reimplementation, though the paper does not mention availability of code or datasets.

clarity.justification: The paper presents a well-structured approach with clear methodology and appropriate claims about competitive performance against more advanced monitors.

topical_fit.justification: Directly addresses LLM safety monitoring, a core concern for builders deploying LLMs in production environments.
